chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Salva Sanders' illness and death
summary: On the northwest tour Salva wins at cards and eats little, then sickens and dies around 1936-37, probably of cancer.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: (Side B of Tape 2 begins at this point.)

Now, with Salva Sanders, we were on a tour up in the northwest and you know, like most bands, if we had nothing to do and everything, so after the dance would be over, we'd get to the hotel and the boys would have a poker game, shoot crap or whatever, it was nobody, just the members and Salva was a pretty good little hustler with the cards, and most times would win, and very conservative. A lot of times when he won he would give me money to keep, and the guys would kid him, because it looked like he wasn't eating very much, and of course they would say, what are you doing, starving yourself, because he began to lose weight.
Over how long a period was this?
He was saying he just wasn't hungry, and I'm quite sure he wasn't. I guess maybe about three or four months, when

we got back into Tulsa, Salva bought a car and everything was around, and then just all of a sudden, he just got down, and we got specialists and everything. At first we thought he had a cold and they checked and no, it wasn't tuberculosis. He just went down, and a little time passed. I think now undoubtedly it must have been cancer, and he did smoke an awful lot, but cancer wasn't known then. But we lost Salva.
I believe that must have been around about thirty six or seven.
